questions.question: When does an async read/list refusal surface?

options.label: Split by I/O (Recommended)
options.description: Pure refusals (InvalidPath, closed guard, capability) raise at the call; I/O-derived ones (NotFound) at first iteration. No public API break; spec states the split explicitly.

options.label: All at the call
options.description: Every refusal before the iterator is returned. Requires `await store.read()` style coroutine-returning-iterator: breaking async API change, CHANGELOG + migration note.

options.label: Keep lazy, just state it
options.description: Everything at first iteration, as today. Cheapest; documents current behaviour, guide and ASYNC-006 amended. Async/sync timing stays asymmetric.

questions.question: Who owns a caller-supplied content iterator the kernel abandons (BK-448)?

options.label: Kernel acloses it (Recommended)
options.description: Whoever stops consuming closes, matching SEEK-011 and the aclosing convention. Fixes BUG-335's 4 routes; finally runs on the right loop.

options.label: Caller owns it
options.description: BE-030/ASYNC spec says the caller must aclose; kernel does nothing. No code change, but every caller must wrap in aclosing() and GC-time finally stays possible.

questions.question: A read stream's close fails after the read itself succeeded (T5). What happens, in both runtimes?

options.label: Suppress + log + liveness (Rec.)
options.description: Data was delivered; close failure is logged, fed to connection_dead so a Session can condemn the connection, never raised. When the read also failed, the read error wins. Sync already behaves so; async read and read_bytes change.

options.label: Raise mapped
options.description: Close failure raises RemoteStoreError in both runtimes; read_bytes discards bytes it already read. Strictest, but turns cleanup noise into data loss for the caller.

questions.question: How far does BK-449 state the Session half, given no remote driver exists to measure?

options.label: Decide owners, defer states (Rec.)
options.description: Now: backend, stream, handle, iterator states (measurable on Memory + fake) and the Session exit owners incl. stream-outlives-run. Session's state set finalised and pinned in the D3 step-2 PR against S3Boto3.

options.label: Full Session states now
options.description: Unconnected/connected/condemned/reconnecting specified and modelled from D5's design text before step 2. Meets the 'due before' literally; risk of revising it at step 2.

options.label: Split into two items
options.description: BK-449 keeps the session-less protocol; a new item owns the Session protocol, due with step 2. Cleaner scope, one more backlog item and dossier.

options.label: Adopt as stated (Recommended)

Stream on an invalidated client (Gemini #1): what does the protocol state?

options.label: Drop lease, close now (Recommended)
options.description: invalidate closes the client immediately; its streams fail mapped on next read. connection_dead must mean transport-level death, not a channel error. Simplest, true for SFTP and S3.

options.label: Keep lease
options.description: Condemned client closes after its last stream releases. More code, only helps a client that is condemned yet still able to serve, which the dead-verdict excludes.

questions.question: Cancellation inside Session.run (Gemini #2)?

options.label: Never invalidate (Recommended)
options.description: Cancel takes the failure exits and re-raises; socket hygiene is the SDK pool's. Only async remote is Azure, whose pool already discards half-read connections.

options.label: Invalidate if socket dirty
options.description: Gemini's B. Needs a driver signal for 'mid-transmission' that no SDK exposes; driver authors would guess.

options.label: Invalidate always
options.description: My earlier proposal. Safe but causes reconnect storms on routine timeouts.

questions.question: Integrity failures near stream end (Gemini #4)?

options.label: End-of-data driver rule (Rec.)
options.description: Driver signals exhaustion only after its integrity check passed, so integrity = read failure. Close errors after exhaustion stay cleanup (suppress, log, liveness). No error taxonomy.

options.label: Cleanup vs integrity split
options.description: Gemini's B: classify each close error. Every driver must sort its SDK's close exceptions into two buckets; misclassification silently drops one.

questions.question: Concurrent-overwrite conflict (Gemini #6): where does it go?

options.label: Timing in 449, mapping in 450 (Rec.)
options.description: BK-449 states it surfaces at commit for open_write, at the call for put; BK-450 owns the classify mapping to AlreadyExists. Add a row to each item.

options.label: Both in BK-449
options.description: One place, but pulls fault-taxonomy work into the state protocol and widens an L item.

Concurrent close vs in-flight operations (Gemini #1): which rule?

options.label: Atomic accessor, no wait (Rec.)
options.description: Client create/teardown is atomic against the closed flag (mutex around the accessor only, never held over I/O; async re-checks after the connect await and closes a client born after close). close never waits for in-flight ops; driver teardown must wake blocked calls, which then fail mapped. Owner: Session (remote), kernel (session-less).

options.label: Reader-writer lock
options.description: Gemini's rule: ops hold a read lock, close takes the write lock. Airtight, but close blocks behind every in-flight op, so one hung read hangs close.

questions.question: A failed abort after a failed commit (Gemini #4 residue)?

options.label: Log + liveness (Rec.)
options.description: Same as stream close: the commit error is raised, the abort failure logged and fed to connection_dead. Driver obligation: abort legal after a failed commit and idempotent. S3 docs name the lifecycle backstop.

options.label: Raise abort failure
options.description: Surface the leak to the caller. Masks the commit error, which is the one that says why the write failed.

questions.question: unwrap() after invalidate (proposal A, unchallenged): what does it do?

options.label: Reconnect via run (Rec.)
options.description: Consistent with 'next run reconnects' and D5's 'unwrap goes through run'. A caller holding the old client keeps a dead object; stated in BE-022.

options.label: Raise until next operation
options.description: unwrap never triggers I/O; returns the client only when one is live. Caller must run an op first: surprising, and adds a Session state.

options.label: With the handle item (Rec.)
options.description: BK-449 states the rule (spec 003 BE-033, with today's per-layer timing recorded as the gap). The new user.api item implements timing at all sites plus the read handle: one behaviour-change PR, one CHANGELOG/migration story.

options.label: In BK-449
options.description: BK-449 also moves pure refusals to the call at ~13 sites both runtimes. Rule and code land together; PR grows well beyond 'single-site fixes'.
